findings.title: Max Voter Weight Manipulation
findings.description: The vulnerability arises because the maximum voter weight in the Pyth governance system is calculated using the total supply of the governing token mint, which is manipulatable. The root cause is that the total supply can be artificially inflated during voting and then reduced (via token burning) before proposal finalization, thereby altering the voting threshold. An attacker can exploit this by locking a significant portion of tokens (e.g., 33%), initiating an unlock, voting during the pre-unlock phase when their weight is high, and then burning tokens after voting but before finalization. This reduces the total supply, causing their vote to represent a higher percentage of the new, lower supply, potentially pushing a proposal over the required threshold. The impact is severe: an attacker could pass malicious proposals, including those that grant them control or allow minting additional tokens, leading to potential loss of funds and governance takeover.
